chapter: California, Art Tatum and Lionel Hampton
title: Leaving for New York via Buffalo and Stuff Smith's players
summary: Deciding to go solo, he stopped in Buffalo, heard George Clark, Jonah Jones and Stuff Smith's group, and played a six-piece show band at $22 a week.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: But here for the first time I had musicians who could read well and interpret the music and play it, and so I do remember one song in particular I wrote. An original called "Train Time Dorraine." But any way, as I said, I finally left the band and went on -- I decided that I should try to do

something on my own, and I decided to go to New York. And I stopped over in Buffalo where I played with a group of musicians there. George Clark who had been with Stuff Smith, the violinist. In fact I had heard him, they had a great small band, one of the finest small bands I'd ever heard in my life. But they were mainly entertainers also, but they played good music. George Clark played tenor saxophone, and Jonah Jones played the trumpet. He was in that band. And they were quite something. Stuff Smith was a genius on the violin, and--
Oh, yeah, he was a great entertainer and great player, and oh, they were really great. I enjoyed their music many times when they were playing.
Cozy Cole was a drummer, yes.

So any way I spent a little time around Buffalo, and I played with some of the musicians who I had played with with Omaha, Nebraska, in Omaha, Nebraska, including that drummer Debo Mills. We played out there at a place called [Bardos.] They had a lot of shows, and we played these shows with this six piece band, and tried to play our little jazz music inbetween, for $22.00 a week. You know.
